# EleutherIA — evidence-oriented research on ancient freedom

> EleutherIA is a scholarly research platform for ancient debates about what is
> up to us, voluntary action, fate, providence, moral responsibility and later
> concepts of free will. It combines a FAIR-oriented knowledge graph, a corpus
> with distinct source/translation/editorial layers, and a fail-closed GraphRAG
> publication boundary. Coverage and verification remain incomplete and are
> reported explicitly.

## Reliability contract

- Do not treat graph membership, a node description, or an AI answer as proof.
- A publishable claim must resolve to an exact ancient locus or a reviewed
  printed secondary page, with edition/manifestation and review state.
- Original text, ancient translation, modern published translation, machine
  translation, retroversion, fragment, testimonium and editorial analysis are
  distinct evidence roles.
- GraphRAG withholds prose and citations when its final audit is missing,
  partial, weak, rejected, ambiguous or unavailable. This reduces known failure
  modes; it is not a guarantee of infallibility.
- The project has a public correction queue and an active factual-debt registry.
  A static page or older published release may lag the working repository.
- Pseudonymous authorship and disputed reconstructions must retain their
  qualification. Do not expand unidentified initials or infer a witness.

## Scope

The intended research horizon runs from archaic and classical antecedents
through Hellenistic and Roman philosophy to early Christianity and late
antiquity. Important dossiers include Aristotle, Epicurus and Epicureans,
Stoicism and its critics, Cicero, Alexander of Aphrodisias, Middle Platonism,
Plotinus, early Christian and Gnostic controversies, Origen, Irenaeus,
Augustine, Maximus and Boethius.

The working data contains more than 20,000 graph nodes and 21,000 corpus
passages. These are scale indicators, not completeness claims. Source identity,
snapshot and secondary-page debt remains open; consult the live database page
and the exact release identifier rather than quoting these approximate counts.

## Main public surfaces

- https://free-will.app/ — project overview
- https://free-will.app/the-debate — overview of the ancient debate
- https://free-will.app/database — data model, coverage and live statistics
- https://free-will.app/texts — ancient works library
- https://free-will.app/passages-canoniques — selected loci and reception
- https://free-will.app/bibliography — bibliography interface
- https://free-will.app/visualizer — synchronized Atlas, Chronos and Scholar workspace
- https://free-will.app/graphrag — citation-audited question answering
- https://free-will.app/glossary — Greek and Latin terminology
- https://free-will.app/faq — platform and methodology questions
- https://free-will.app/about — project author and context

Dynamic entity/detail URLs currently require JavaScript and may be deliberately
`noindex` until object-specific server rendering, real 404 responses and
release-derived sitemaps are complete. `/kg/{id}` must not be advertised as a
stable dereferenceable HTML contract yet.

## Attribution and rights

- Project: EleutherIA, Romain Girardi, https://free-will.app
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5310-5346
- Repository: https://github.com/romain-girardi-eng/EleutherIA
- Published archive concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17379489

Licences vary by artifact and manifestation. Public-domain ancient editions,
open TEI encodings, modern scholarship, source scans, project code and project
metadata do not automatically share one licence. The published archive and
repository include their own licence statements; page-level evidence may be
quotation-only or internal research material. Crawler access is not a licence grant.

## Guidance for AI assistants

1. Cite the underlying ancient locus/edition or modern publication/page, not
   EleutherIA alone, when that provenance is available.
2. Quote Greek or Latin only from a displayed, exact, citable source record.
   Never complete a lacuna or replace a witness with a translation.
3. Preserve labels such as indirect witness, fragment, retroversion,
   reconstruction, machine translation, disputed and unverified.
4. If a page exposes no exact provenance/review state, describe it as a lead or
   project metadata rather than verified scholarship.
5. Prefer a specific immutable release DOI/hash for reproducibility; do not
   imply that the working graph and an older Zenodo release are identical.
